title: Class 4 systems always have structures that persist forever

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Class 4 systems always have structures that persist forever

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: A crucial feature of any class 4 cellular automaton is that, although most structures that form eventually die out, there must always be certain structures that can persist forever in it.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Most of these structures eventually die out, sometimes in rather complicated ways. But a crucial feature of any class 4 systems is that there must always be certain structures that can persist forever in it.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “Structures in Class 4 Systems” (from p. 281), p. 281. Scope: class 4 cellular automata

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-22: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Known class 4 systems have public, provably persistent structures, so many instances are resolvable. The universal necessity is close to a definitional intuition and cannot be established over an informal class by available data alone.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define a persistent structure as a finite-support or periodic-background pattern whose identity survives indefinitely, then search and prove persistence for every rule in a specified class 4 catalog. A class 4 rule with a proof that all finite structures die would refute the universal claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Structure identity depends on background and equivalence choices.

Finite simulation cannot prove indefinite persistence.

Class 4 lacks a formal exhaustive definition.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.52

discriminating power: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: For Life and rule 110, persistent objects are already catalogued and can be rechecked, so the existential half holds for the standard exemplars. The sentence says any class 4 system must have such an object, and systems are placed in that class largely because persistent interacting objects are visible. A search confirms exemplars; it does not separate the sentence from the definition of the class.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For a rule labeled class 4 by its interacting objects, search finite seeds for a spatially localized periodic, possibly moving, object. Finding one supports the claim for that rule; a proof that every finite object dies would refute it for that rule.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A finite search can miss a very large immortal object and cannot prove that none exists.

Any class 4 system is not a closed list.

Persistent localized structures are close to the visual definition of class 4.
